assertions.description: HTMLIFrameElement.prototype exposes the connectionAllowlist reflected IDL attribute (spec §4.1).
The IDL attribute reflects the content attribute: setAttribute('connectionallowlist', v) is readable as element.connectionAllowlist.
Writing element.connectionAllowlist sets the content attribute (reflection, IDL to content).
Sec-Required-Connection-Allowlist is a forbidden request header (Sec- prefix): a page-constructed Request cannot carry it.
Prerequisite machinery: the allowlist grammar resolves members via URL patterns, so the URLPattern engine the spec builds on must exist.

An enforcing user agent sends Sec-Required-Connection-Allowlist with the navigation request of a frame whose embedder set connectionallowlist (verified live by the surface-probe concept's same-origin echo route).
assertions.test: Needs a build with the ConnectionAllowlistEmbeddedEnforcement runtime flag (--enable-experimental-web-platform-features); no released Chrome ships it (ChromeStatus desktop milestone: None). Observe via /v157/connection-allowlists-embedded-enforcement/surface-probe/.

assertions.description: A framed document that returns neither a satisfying Connection-Allowlist nor Allow-Connection-Allowlist-From is blocked (handshake-lab scenario C).
assertions.test: Needs an enforcing build; in baseline browsers the frame loads unrestricted, which the handshake-lab records honestly. Observe via /v157/connection-allowlists-embedded-enforcement/handshake-lab/.

assertions.description: A framed document opting in via Allow-Connection-Allowlist-From naming the embedder origin loads, with the requirement applied to its connections (handshake-lab scenario B; header compared byte-for-byte like Allow-CSP-From).
assertions.test: Needs an enforcing build. The header itself is genuinely served by this site's _server.ts widget route and inspectable via same-origin fetch in the lab.

assertions.description: Inside a frame enforced under a PATH-SCOPED allowlist, a fetch to an endpoint matching no allowlist pattern is blocked before the connection (the widget’s blocked/ping fetch).
assertions.test: Needs an enforcing build AND a path-scoped policy: the default requirement ‘("https://good.example" response-origin)’ permits BOTH same-origin pings, so it can never block blocked/ping. Load the widget with its ?allowlist= override, e.g. /v157/connection-allowlists-embedded-enforcement/widget?optin=satisfy&allowlist=("https://good.example" "<this-origin>/v157/connection-allowlists-embedded-enforcement/allowed/*") (substitute the deployed origin), framed by an embedder requiring that same list. Expected: allowed/ping succeeds, blocked/ping is blocked before connection. In baseline browsers both fetches succeed, which the widget labels as the unrestricted baseline.
